correspondence.component_scope: Headward tributary corridor southwest and east of Cerro Tuzgle
correspondence.finding: The selected opening is a small headward feeder southwest of Tuzgle. The original map shows it entering the Pirca valley, turning east toward Charco and then north along the Charco valley. This is not the separate San Antonio de los Cobres drainage farther east.
correspondence.correspondence: supported at ordinary valley/corridor scale; no exact source spring or first feeder-name boundary assigned
correspondence.mapped_component_name: Quebrada de Pirca / Quebrada de Charco

correspondence.component_scope: Los Charcos and upper Pastos Chicos transition
correspondence.finding: The northgoing headward corridor continues through the mapped Los Charcos drainage east of Puesto Sey. The map distinguishes the Sijes/Agua Blanca/Sepultura drainage to its west, and shows its junction with the northgoing Pastos Chicos corridor toward Pastos Chicos village. The selected path is not assigned all western tributary names.

correspondence.component_scope: Pastos Chicos–Huancar–Susques trunk
correspondence.finding: The selected route follows the northgoing Pastos Chicos valley through the village and Huancar toward Susques. Named side valleys remain distinct. No intervening lake or reservoir passage is depicted.

correspondence.component_scope: Susques-area junction and Las Burras gorge
correspondence.finding: The map shows the Pastos Chicos corridor turning east by Susques, receiving the northern drainage and continuing through Aguadita and Angosto de las Burras. Official provincial prose identifies the formative northern tributary as Coranzulí. The resulting eastward river is labeled Río de las Burras, also receiving the Barrancas drainage farther east.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Las Burras fan toward Salinas Grandes and saline northward connector
correspondence.finding: Beyond the Cerro Negro vicinity the selected route swings southeast across the broad lower fan to the northern/western Salinas Grandes margin, then turns east and north along the low saline belt toward Guayatayoc. The original250k map instead depicts the named Las Burras river taking a more direct eastward path north of this excursion. It depicts the fan and saline depressions, but not a continuous channel on the selected excursion. The100k image contains no map coverage. Neither the CFI basin figure nor provincial prose closes this connector.
correspondence.correspondence: material connector unresolved; regional basin association is insufficient

correspondence.component_scope: Actual terminal setting
correspondence.finding: The retained terminal lies within the mapped Guayatayoc saline/lacustrine depression, northeast of Rinconadillas and north of Salinas Grandes. It is an endorheic receiving setting, not an ocean outlet, and no separate reservoir or downstream river exit is depicted. This receiving identity does not prove the preceding selected lower-fan pathway.
correspondence.correspondence: receiving setting supported; continuous approach remains conditional on unresolved lower connector

correspondence.component_scope: Actual selected far-headward reach and Prensa junction
correspondence.finding: The Lamarão original depicts the selected small headward drainage east of the Jibóia/Matão setting and west of Laranjeiras. Its southeast trend runs toward the Prensa junction rather than the more easterly Carima or Salitre branches. The Santa Bárbara original overlaps that junction and expressly describes Prensa entering Salgado, then follows the receiving river toward Sítio das Flores/Desterro. The far-headward line itself is not given a secure hydronym.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at generalized headwater and junction-component scale
correspondence.name_scope: Prensa is the joining western branch; Salgado is supported on the connected downstream upper corridor. The unnamed selected first reach is not automatically assigned either tributary or representative downstream name.
correspondence.lake_reservoir_setting: Small nearby ponds are shown around the Jibóia setting; the selected headward route is a stream corridor, with no required major through-lake or impoundment passage depicted.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper Salgado corridor east of Santa Bárbara and west of Santanópolis
correspondence.finding: The original sheets follow the same south-trending river from Desterro/Mocambo past the Salitre confluence and Boa Espera, then along Salgadinho, Salgado and the western side of Santanópolis. The Sítio da Luzia, Azeitona/Poços-side and smaller junctions remain side drainage. The selected river continues south past Roça do Rio and east of Tiquaruçu, through the Sítio–Candeia Grossa/Jacu setting, overlapping the northern Coração de Maria map.
correspondence.name_scope: Upper-corridor source label only; not a declaration that the entire selected system is Salgado.

correspondence.component_scope: Coração de Maria western and southern Pojuca bend
correspondence.finding: Coração de Maria original labels the selected western receiving river Rio Pojuca past Jaíba/Itacava and São Roque. It continues south along the Feira de Santana side, rounds the broad southern bend adjoining Conceição do Jacuípe and turns east/northeast before returning southeast. The Paramerim-side connection is a tributary junction; the selected route stays on the mapped Pojuca receiving channel rather than switching to the stream through Coração de Maria town.
correspondence.name_scope: Named receiving corridor. No exact name-transition point from Salgado to Pojuca is asserted.
correspondence.lake_reservoir_setting: Lagoa do Peixe and other named small lakes in the surrounding sheet are off the selected through-route; no major selected lake chain is depicted.

correspondence.component_scope: Teodoro Sampaio–Terra Nova connector and middle-river turn
correspondence.finding: The overlapping Teodoro Sampaio and Terra Nova originals depict the Pojuca receiving reach with Ingazeira, Sapé and Camurujipe connections, then the southward approach past Barra/Olhos d’Água and Mucuri toward Terra Nova. Rio Frio is shown joining from the west. The main river passes the town setting and turns east toward the Pitanga confluence on the Catu side. This explicitly supplies the selected west-to-east middle connection.
correspondence.name_scope: Names in component_names_observed refer to separate tributary/connector settings as depicted, not whole-system aliases.
correspondence.lake_reservoir_setting: Lagoa do Iassu on the northern Teodoro Sampaio sheet is on a side drainage and is not traversed by the selected route. No large selected reservoir passage is depicted.

correspondence.component_scope: Catu southern boundary and Pojuca town reach
correspondence.finding: The Catu original follows the selected receiving river east from the Pitanga-side setting through Banco de Areia and the Bela Flor-side corridor, then past the southern Catu/São Sebastião do Passé context and Muritiba to Pojuca. The named Rio Catu approaches from the north and joins the Pojuca receiving reach; it is not the selected upstream branch. The overlapping Pojuca and Mata de São João originals continue the same main river eastward beyond town.

correspondence.component_scope: Quiricó junctions, floodplain and Pedra do Salgado bend
correspondence.finding: Pojuca and Mata de São João originals follow the eastward selected channel through the Quiricó Pequeno/Rio Fundo confluence settings and Buri floodplain. It then bends northeast toward the Quiricó Grande connection and Pedra do Salgado before turning southeast. The adjacent Juruaba drainage is separately depicted; the selected river stays on the Pojuca receiving channel.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at generalized main-river and floodplain scale
correspondence.lake_reservoir_setting: The map shows broad flood-prone and wet-ground river margins near Buri. These are a connected river/floodplain component, not evidence for a named through-lake chain.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower southward Pojuca and actual Atlantic terminal
correspondence.finding: The Mata de São João original shows the selected southward continuation through Castanheira, Juruaba and Vargem de Baixo, then the Mucugê and Tiririca river corridor. It continues past the Itapecerica-side tributary setting to the lower meanders at Barra do Pojuca. The source draws the mouth into the Atlantic immediately south of Praia do Forte, with the coastal wet-ground setting on the opposite side. This establishes the actual selected terminal component independently of the model sea class.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary lower-river and terminal-component scale
correspondence.lake_reservoir_setting: Coastal floodplain/wet-ground and a widened final channel are mapped. No unresolved through-reservoir connector remains.
correspondence.terminal_setting: Atlantic river-mouth corridor at Barra do Pojuca, beside and south of Praia do Forte; generalized historical mouth/coast setting, not an exact present-day opening or bank-position claim.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern headward approach
correspondence.finding: The fixed selected model begins in the western MacAlpine map-area and initially proceeds north with small bends. Actual headwater setting, any starting lake and the selected opening connector have not been established from read original cartography. This description of orientation is not source correspondence.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper eastward displacement, westward bend and northern return
correspondence.finding: The selected model bends east and then returns west before continuing north and northeast. The regional1994 figure does not resolve the intervening lake passages, tributary junctions or this branch choice. Neither MacAlpine Lake nor Perry River is assigned merely from regional proximity or a neighboring completed finding.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle northwestward bend and northward continuation
correspondence.finding: A northwestward deviation and subsequent north/northeast continuation are present in the fixed selected model. No inspected detailed original map establishes these connecting channels, major waterbody passages or material incoming junctions. General parallel northward rivers in the primary field-study figure are insufficient to close the gap.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower northeastward river corridor and minor reversals
correspondence.finding: The selected lower corridor trends northeast, with several northward reaches and westward reversals. The original regional figure distinguishes this western coastal sector from the named Perry River farther east, but does not securely identify this entire selected river or its junctions and waterbody links.

correspondence.component_scope: Final northeastward approach and actual coastal terminal
correspondence.finding: The fixed selected terminal lies on the Queen Maud Gulf coastal sector west of Atkinson Point. ARC403 and the original1994 figure supply broad coastal orientation and distinguish Perry River at Chester Bay farther east. Neither establishes the actual selected mouth branch, its relationship to nearby unnamed rivers, or a particular bay name. The colony68 mouth in the neighboring r91 context is not substituted for this endpoint.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected mainstem FID 10639
correspondence.finding: The selected west-to-north and then east/northeast river arc is recognisable as Wawa on the original2014 map and historical Bocay map. The short selected opening extends south of the headward channel shown by the basin atlas; the historical sheet and broad2014 source-region prose do not establish that opening or its approach to the mapped Wawa. The remainder continues around the prominent northern bend and east through tributary junctions toward FID10640.
correspondence.material_gap: Actual selected initial feeder/connection, rather than the name of a small already-corresponded tributary.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected mainstem FID 10640
correspondence.finding: Original2014 cartography traces the eastern Wawa continuation, the major Likus junction from the north, and the turn south through the lowland main river to the following fragment. The historical Punta Gorda sheet independently maps the Wawa corridor and its southward progression; it is supplementary historical evidence.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected mainstem FID 10641
correspondence.finding: The lower southward Wawa corridor receives the Siksikwas-side drainage and enters the linked Karatá coastal-lagoon setting before the common outlet toward the Caribbean by Wawa. The1997 original schematic distinguishes Yulu, Kuth Pura, Lamlaya and Wark Wark links around the same estuary. It supports the river–lagoon–outlet relationship rather than treating each lagoon or modeled water crossing as a reach named Wawa. No reservoir is shown in the inspected selected corridor.
correspondence.boundary_limit: Exact modern lagoon banks, mouth vertices and channels are not assigned from historical/schematic maps.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected tributary FID 10642
correspondence.finding: The selected southwestern side chain is the southeastern-trending Kukalaya corridor, with mapped side tributaries, continuing into the opening portion of FID10643. It is geographically distinct from Wawa. The independent regional sources describe Kukalaya’s principal downstream destination as Wouhta/Wounta, so this selected chain cannot simply inherit the Wawa hydronym.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected tributary FID 10643
correspondence.finding: Its western opening continues along Kukalaya and turns east across the lowland corridor. Its northeastern final portion approaches the Wark Wark–Karatá estuarine system and shares the final lagoon/outlet setting with the mainstem. The1997 field-study prose explicitly describes a Slim Slim Bila link between Kukalaya and Wark Wark and broader lagoon connections, but the original figures and the2014 regional map do not continuously correspond the selected intervening east/northeast transfer. The historical Prinzapolka sheet separately depicts Cucalaya and Workwok without closing that specific transfer.
correspondence.material_gap: Actual selected inter-river/lowland connector coverage and resulting flow continuity, not merely uncertainty in its label.
